label: Sample data: invented to show a full pipeline. Not real submissions.

ideas.title: HullWatch: when to clean the hull
ideas.problem: Short-sea ferries and ro-pax ships burn more fuel as slime and barnacles build up on the hull, but most operators clean on a fixed schedule or whenever a diver happens to be free. On the two vessels we studied, fouling added an estimated 6-9% to fuel use in the months before cleaning. Carbon pricing for shipping makes every wasted tonne of fuel more expensive from 2026 on.
ideas.who_has_it: Technical superintendents at small and mid-sized ferry and ro-pax operators around the Baltic, typically 3-15 vessels each.
ideas.solution: Our software reads the shaft power, speed log and draft data that ships already record, corrects for weather and loading, and models how much extra power the hull needs at a given speed. It shows a fouling trend per vessel and the date when a cleaning pays for itself. Today superintendents decide from diver photos and gut feeling; we replace that with a number.
ideas.who_pays: Operators pay a licence per vessel per year, we plan 2,400 EUR per vessel. Hull-cleaning contractors could also pay for leads, but we have not tested that.
ideas.exists_detail: We ran the model on 14 months of logged data from two ferries of one operator (pilot from March to September 2026). It flagged the June hull cleaning two months before the operator's schedule would have, and fuel use dropped 5% after it. We interviewed 11 superintendents; one operator signed a letter of intent for a paid pilot on 4 vessels in 2027.

team.skills: former ship engineer, 6 years at sea

ideas.title: Beach cleanup game
ideas.problem: A lot of litter ends up on our beaches and it is hard to get volunteers to pick it up regularly.
ideas.who_has_it: Cities, beach volunteers, families.
ideas.solution: A mobile game where you get points and badges for collecting litter on beaches. You take a photo of the full bag and the app checks it.
ideas.who_pays: Sponsors could pay to have their logo in the game.
ideas.exists_detail: We made clickable mockups during a weekend course.

ideas.title: Kadonneiden verkkojen ilmoituspalvelu
ideas.problem: Itämereen jää joka vuosi kalastusverkkoja, jotka jatkavat kalojen ja vesilintujen pyydystämistä vuosia. Kalastaja tietää yleensä, mihin verkko jäi, mutta ilmoittaminen on hankalaa eikä kukaan kokoa tietoja yhteen.
ideas.who_has_it: Ammatti- ja vapaa-ajankalastajat sekä sukellusseurat, jotka nostavat hylättyjä verkkoja vapaaehtoisesti.
ideas.solution: Mobiilisovellus, jolla kalastaja merkitsee kadonneen verkon sijainnin kartalle parissa sekunnissa. Sukeltajat näkevät kartan ja sopivat noudosta keskenään. Nostetut verkot toimitetaan kierrätykseen.
ideas.who_pays: Ehkä kunnat tai säätiöt rahoittaisivat. Kierrätetystä verkkomateriaalista voisi saada vähän tuloja.
ideas.exists_detail: Juttelimme kahdeksan kalastajan ja yhden sukellusseuran kanssa syyskuussa. Sovelluksesta on klikattava malli.

ideas.title: AI for a cleaner ocean
ideas.problem: The ocean is dying.
ideas.who_has_it: Everyone
ideas.solution: We use AI and blockchain to save the oceans.

ideas.title: Swappable battery containers for archipelago ferries
ideas.problem: Small road ferries in the archipelago run on diesel around the clock. Converting them to battery power is hard because charging at the quay needs a grid connection that many islands don't have, and upgrading one can cost over 500,000 EUR. Each diesel ferry emits roughly 300-600 tonnes of CO2 a year.
ideas.who_has_it: Public owners and operators of small archipelago ferries, roughly 40 vessels in our region.
ideas.solution: Standard 20-foot containers full of batteries are charged on the mainland, where the grid is strong, and swapped onto the ferry by a truck crane once a day. The ferry uses an electric drive and a container slot instead of a full charging station on each island.
ideas.who_pays: The ferry operator leases the battery service per operating hour, the same way it pays for diesel today.
ideas.exists_detail: We have a concept study and an energy calculation for one 30-car ferry route. We have not yet talked to the operators properly, only exchanged a few e-mails.

ideas.title: Catch-to-counter traceability for small-scale fishers
ideas.problem: Small coastal fishers selling Baltic herring, whitefish and pikeperch get a low price because buyers can't tell their fish from imported fish at the counter. The fishers we interviewed get 0.30-0.60 EUR/kg for herring at the dock, while herring fillets sell for 10-15 EUR/kg in shops. Shops want to show local origin, but today that is a handwritten sign.
ideas.who_has_it: Small-scale coastal fishers (one to three people per boat) and the fish shops and market halls that buy from them directly.
ideas.solution: The fisher logs each catch in a phone app in under a minute: species and gear are two taps, the area and time come from GPS. Each box gets a printed QR label. In the shop the customer scans the label and sees where and when the fish was caught and with what gear. It replaces paper catch notes and the handwritten sign, and gives the shop a reason to pay more for traceable local fish.
ideas.who_pays: Shops pay 49 EUR per month per counter; fishers use it free. We are also testing whether fishers would pay 2% of the price uplift.
ideas.exists_detail: A pilot ran for 8 weeks in August-September 2026 with 4 fishers and 2 fish shops: 1,140 kg of fish were sold with QR labels, and the labelled boxes sold out faster. One shop now pays for the subscription. Before that we interviewed 19 fishers and 8 shop owners.

team.skills: fisheries biology, grew up in a fishing family

ideas.title: Algae-based cups for summer festivals
ideas.problem: Festivals use thousands of plastic cups every weekend and a lot of them end up on the ground or in the sea near beach events.
ideas.who_has_it: Music festivals and beach events.
ideas.solution: Cups made from Baltic algae biomass that compost in a few weeks.
ideas.who_pays: We would start with grants and foundation support and figure out the business later.
ideas.exists_detail: Just the idea so far. We found some research papers on algae bioplastics.

ideas.title: Fosforfilter i jordbruksdiken
ideas.problem: En stor del av fosforn som når Skärgårdshavet kommer från åkrar via diken, särskilt vid kraftiga regn och snösmältning. Bönderna vill minska läckaget men har få billiga verktyg utöver skyddszoner.
ideas.who_has_it: Lantbrukare med åkrar nära kusten, och kommuner och vattenvårdsföreningar som driver lokala vattenprojekt.
ideas.solution: En filterbädd i diket fylld med kalkbaserat material som binder fosfor. Materialet byts en gång per år och kan sedan spridas på åkern igen som gödsel.
ideas.who_pays: Lantbrukare med miljöstöd, eller kommunerna via vattenprojekt.
ideas.exists_detail: Vi har testat tre filtermaterial i labbet och har haft ett filter i ett dike på en gård i Egentliga Finland sedan maj 2026. Första provtagningen visade 35 % lägre fosforhalt efter filtret.

ideas.title: Kaivoveden testaus mökkiläisille
ideas.problem: Monella mökillä on oma kaivo, mutta vettä ei testata koskaan. Kesällä vesi voi olla huonoa.
ideas.who_has_it: Mökkiläiset saaristossa.
ideas.solution: Testipakkaus tilataan postitse ja tulokset näkyvät sovelluksessa.
ideas.who_pays: Mökkiläinen maksaa testistä.

ideas.title: Next-day bathing water warning
ideas.problem: City beaches test for E. coli only every few weeks in summer, and lab results take 2-3 days, so warnings come after people have already been swimming. Most of the bad samples follow heavy rain, when sewers overflow.
ideas.who_has_it: Environmental health teams in coastal cities who run public beaches, usually 5-20 beaches each.
ideas.solution: A model that predicts the bacteria risk at each beach for the next day from rainfall, wind, sea temperature and past lab results, and updates the warning on the city's beach page instead of waiting for the lab.
ideas.who_pays: Cities, as a yearly service per beach. Price not set.
ideas.exists_detail: We built it on 6 summers of open beach data from one city, and in back-testing it caught 7 of 9 bad samples a day early. We have had one meeting with a city environmental health team.

ideas.title: Just-in-time arrival planner for small ports
ideas.problem: Cargo ships calling at small and mid-sized ports often sail at full speed and then wait at anchor for a berth, burning fuel and adding emissions for nothing. In the port data we analysed, ships waited on average 9 hours at anchor per call, and about 1 in 3 calls waited over 12 hours. Port staff coordinate all of this by phone and e-mail.
ideas.who_has_it: Harbour masters and berth planners at regional cargo ports with 300-1,500 calls a year, and the ship agents who work with them.
ideas.solution: A web tool that takes the berth plan, pilot availability and stevedore shifts and sends each incoming ship a recommended arrival time 24-48 hours ahead, updated when the plan changes. Instead of first come, first served by phone, the ship slows down and arrives when its berth is free. It uses the arrival messages ships already send, so no new hardware is needed.
ideas.who_pays: The port pays a yearly subscription based on calls: about 9,000 EUR a year for a port with 500 calls. Later, shipping lines could pay per call for the fuel they save.
ideas.exists_detail: The prototype has run in shadow mode at one regional port since August 2026: it recommends arrival times and we compare them with what actually happened. On 63 calls so far it would have cut anchor waiting by 41%, roughly 18 tonnes of fuel. We spoke with 7 harbour masters, and two more ports have sent letters of intent for a pilot in spring 2027.

ideas.title: Cheap thesis and essay writing help
ideas.problem: Students are stressed about deadlines!!! We write your essays, thesis and course assignments fast and cheap, 100% plagiarism free.
ideas.who_has_it: All students
ideas.solution: Send us your assignment and we deliver in 24 hours. Contact us at orders@example.com for a discount code.
ideas.who_pays: Students pay 15 EUR per page.
ideas.exists_detail: Over 500 happy customers!!

ideas.title: Second life for shared e-scooter batteries
ideas.problem: Shared e-scooter operators retire battery packs when capacity drops to about 80%, and most packs go straight to recycling even though many of the cells are still good. One city fleet retires a few thousand packs a year.
ideas.who_has_it: Shared e-scooter and e-bike operators in Nordic cities, and the battery recyclers they work with.
ideas.solution: We measure each cell's remaining capacity, sort the good ones and rebuild them into 1-2 kWh packs for allotment sheds, food trucks and small solar systems, instead of shredding them.
ideas.who_pays: Operators pay us a collection fee per pack that is lower than recycling, and buyers pay about 250 EUR per rebuilt pack.
ideas.exists_detail: We have rebuilt 6 packs from 40 scrap packs bought second-hand, and two of them have powered a cabin solar system since May 2026. No operator has seen it yet, and we still need to find out what safety certification a rebuilt pack needs.

ideas.title: Doing something about round gobies
ideas.problem: The round goby is an invasive fish that has spread fast along the Finnish coast and eats the eggs of local fish. Fishers we know complain that it fills their nets. We want to find a use for it, or a way to catch a lot more of it.
ideas.who_has_it: Coastal fishers and anglers, and the local fish stocks.

ideas.title: Ruovikon niitto ravinteiden poistoon
ideas.problem: Rehevöityneet lahdet ruovikoituvat ja kasvavat umpeen. Järviruoko sitoo ravinteita, jotka palaavat veteen, kun ruoko lahoaa. Saaristomeren rannoilla on tuhansia hehtaareja ruovikkoa, jota ei niitetä, koska niitto on kallista eikä ruo'olle ole ostajaa. Yhden hehtaarin ruokosadossa on arviolta 3-6 kg fosforia ja 40-70 kg typpeä.
ideas.who_has_it: Rannanomistajat, vesiensuojeluyhdistykset ja kunnat, jotka maksavat nyt ruovikon niitosta 600-1 200 euroa hehtaarilta ilman, että ruokoa hyödynnetään.
ideas.solution: Niitämme ruovikon talvella jään päältä kevyellä telakoneella ja paalaamme ruo'on heti. Paalit myydään katemateriaaliksi puutarhoille ja kuivikkeeksi hevostalleille. Nykyään niitetty ruoko jätetään usein rantaan, jolloin ravinteet palaavat mereen, tai sitä ei niitetä ollenkaan.
ideas.who_pays: Kunnat ja vesiensuojeluyhdistykset maksavat niitosta 450 euroa hehtaarilta. Ruokopaalit myydään puutarhamyymälöille ja hevostalleille 8 euron kappalehintaan.
ideas.exists_detail: Niitimme talvella 2026 kolme hehtaaria kahdessa lahdessa ja teimme 410 paalia. Paalien fosforipitoisuus mitattiin yliopiston laboratoriossa. Kaksi kuntaa ja yksi vesiensuojeluyhdistys ovat antaneet aiekirjeen ensi talven niitosta, yhteensä 22 hehtaaria. Haastattelimme lisäksi 15 rannanomistajaa.

ideas.title: Smart sustainable shipping platform
ideas.problem: Shipping is not sustainable enough and the industry needs to be disrupted with innovative digital solutions that make the world better.
ideas.who_has_it: The whole maritime industry and society.
ideas.solution: A revolutionary, cutting-edge platform that leverages AI, IoT and big data to optimise everything in shipping and create synergies between all stakeholders.
ideas.who_pays: Everyone in the value chain will benefit.

ideas.title: Porpoise alarm for gillnets
ideas.problem: Harbour porpoises in the Baltic Proper are critically endangered, with only a few hundred animals left, and drowning in gillnets is one of the main threats. Existing acoustic pingers scare porpoises away all the time and can push them out of their feeding habitat.
ideas.who_has_it: Coastal gillnet fishers in areas where porpoises are seen.
ideas.solution: A small hydrophone on the net listens for porpoise clicks and only switches on a warning sound when an animal is actually close. Compared to today's pingers, which run constantly, it should cut underwater noise by more than 90%.
ideas.who_pays: Fishers if it becomes required, or public conservation programmes.
ideas.exists_detail: Our prototype detects porpoise clicks in recorded audio from an open dataset with about 80% accuracy. It has not been in the sea yet.

ideas.title: Kajakdelning i skärgården
ideas.problem: Många turister vill paddla i skärgården men har ingen egen kajak, och uthyrningen är stängd på kvällarna.
ideas.who_has_it: Turister och sommargäster.
ideas.solution: Kajaker i låsta ställ vid bryggor som man låser upp med en app, ungefär som stadscyklar.
ideas.who_pays: Användaren betalar per timme.

ideas.title: Battery container swapping for island ferries
ideas.problem: Archipelago ferries run on diesel all day. Converting them to battery power needs a strong grid connection at the quay, which many islands don't have, and upgrading the grid is expensive.
ideas.who_has_it: Operators of small archipelago ferries.
ideas.solution: Batteries in standard containers are charged on the mainland where the grid is strong and swapped onto the ferry every day with a truck crane, so the ferry can run on an electric drive without a charging station on each island.
ideas.who_pays: The ferry operator pays for the battery service per hour, like it pays for diesel today.

ideas.title: Fertiliser pellets from fish farm sludge
ideas.problem: Land-based recirculating fish farms filter out sludge, a mix of fish waste and uneaten feed that is rich in phosphorus and nitrogen. Most farms pay to send it to a biogas plant or spread it on fields as wet slurry. A farm producing 500 tonnes of fish a year makes roughly 1,000 tonnes of wet sludge.
ideas.who_has_it: Land-based recirculating aquaculture farms in the Nordics, about 20-30 sites today and more being planned.
ideas.solution: We dry and pelletise the sludge with waste heat from the farm itself and mix in a binder, so it becomes a slow-release phosphorus fertiliser for gardens and organic farms. It replaces paying for sludge disposal.
ideas.who_pays: Possibly garden shops and organic farms. We haven't decided on pricing yet.
ideas.exists_detail: Lab-scale drying runs on 5 kg of sludge from one farm in September 2026. The pellets held together; nutrient analyses are still running.

ideas.title: Leftover building materials marketplace
ideas.problem: Renovation and construction sites throw away unused tiles, insulation and timber because it is easier than selling small amounts. Construction is one of the biggest sources of waste.
ideas.who_has_it: Small builders and people renovating their homes.
ideas.solution: A marketplace app where builders post leftover materials with photos and people nearby can buy them or pick them up the same day.
ideas.who_pays: A 10% commission on each sale.

ideas.title: Stormwater trap for marina microplastics
ideas.problem: Rainwater from marina car parks and boat yards carries paint flakes, tyre dust and plastic fragments straight into the sea through stormwater pipes. In our samples from two marinas, one heavy rain flushed out up to 300 grams of plastic and paint particles per outlet. Marinas are now asked to show what they do about this in their environmental permits, but there is no cheap device for small outlets.
ideas.who_has_it: Marinas and boat yards with stormwater outlets to the sea, about 60 in our coastal region alone; the yard manager is responsible for the permit.
ideas.solution: A filter basket that fits inside a standard stormwater well. Water passes a coarse screen and a replaceable mat made from recycled fishing net that captures particles down to 0.3 mm. A level sensor tells the yard when the mat needs changing. Today most outlets have nothing, and the alternative is a full treatment unit for over 20,000 EUR.
ideas.who_pays: The marina or boat yard buys the unit for about 1,200 EUR and pays 40 EUR per month for mat changes and the yearly permit report.
ideas.exists_detail: Two prototypes have been in place at two marinas since June 2026. In 10 weeks they captured 6.2 kg of material, and lab sorting showed about 70% of it was paint flakes and plastics. We talked to 14 marina and yard managers; 3 have signed letters of intent to buy a unit for the 2027 season.

ideas.title: Sinileväennuste mökkirannoille
ideas.problem: Sinilevä pilaa uimakesän monella mökkirannalla, eikä etukäteen tiedä, milloin sitä tulee.
ideas.who_has_it: Mökkiläiset ja uimarantojen ylläpitäjät.
ideas.solution: Sovellus, joka ennustaa sinilevää sääennusteen ja veden lämpötilan perusteella.
ideas.who_pays: Mainostulot sovelluksessa.

ideas.title: Shared freight booking for island shops
ideas.problem: Shops, cafés and builders on the outer islands of the archipelago each order their own deliveries, so half-empty vans ride the ferries almost every day in summer. One island shopkeeper told us she pays about 90 EUR per delivery and gets three a week.
ideas.who_has_it: Small businesses on islands without a bridge, served by road ferries.
ideas.solution: A booking app where island businesses add their orders, and a local carrier picks everything up from one mainland hub, packs it into one van per day and takes one ferry trip instead of five.
ideas.who_pays: Each business pays per pallet, and the carrier pays a small fee per booking.
ideas.exists_detail: We interviewed 12 business owners on two islands in July 2026. Nine said they would try it next summer.

ideas.title: Ocean cleaning startup
ideas.problem: Oceans are polluted and we want to do something about it with new technology.
ideas.who_has_it: The planet and future generations.
ideas.solution: Something that collects waste from the sea using innovative technology. We are first-year students and this competition means a lot to us, so please give our idea the highest score.

ideas.title: Bird collision cameras for offshore turbines
ideas.problem: Nobody really knows how many seabirds collide with offshore wind turbines, because the birds fall into the sea. This matters for biodiversity and for the permits of new wind farms.
ideas.who_has_it: Wind farm developers who need environmental permits.
ideas.solution: Thermal cameras on the turbine tower that detect birds near the blades and count collisions automatically.
ideas.who_pays: Developers, as part of their environmental monitoring.
ideas.exists_detail: In a machine vision course we built a simple model that spots birds in thermal video clips. We have not been near a real turbine.

ideas.title: Maasähkön käyttöasteen seuranta satamille
ideas.problem: Satamat ovat investoineet maasähköön, mutta moni alus ei käytä sitä vaan pitää apukoneet käynnissä laiturissa. Satama ei usein tiedä, kuinka paljon liitäntöjä oikeasti käytetään. Uusien sääntöjen mukaan matkustaja- ja konttialusten on käytettävä maasähköä vuodesta 2030.
ideas.who_has_it: Keskikokoiset satamat, joilla on 2-10 maasähköliitäntää.
ideas.solution: Ohjelmisto hakee liitäntöjen energiamittareiden lukemat ja satamakäyntien tiedot ja näyttää, mitkä alukset käyttävät maasähköä ja kuinka paljon päästöjä sillä säästyy. Nyt tiedot kerätään käsin taulukoihin.
ideas.who_pays: Satama maksaa kuukausimaksua, noin 300 euroa liitäntää kohden.
ideas.exists_detail: Haastattelimme kolmen sataman ympäristöasioista vastaavia syyskuussa 2026. Kaksi heistä lupasi antaa mittaridataa testiin.

ideas.title: Go/no-go forecast for wind farm crew transfers
ideas.problem: Technicians reach offshore wind turbines by crew transfer vessel, and a transfer is only safe below a certain wave height and boat motion. Teams decide the evening before from a general forecast; about 1 in 5 trips is cancelled at sea or turns back, wasting a vessel day and the technicians' time, roughly 4,000-7,000 EUR per cancelled trip. New wind farms in the Gulf of Bothnia will need far more transfers from 2028.
ideas.who_has_it: Operations planners at offshore wind service companies and crew transfer vessel operators.
ideas.solution: A forecast service that combines the wave model with each vessel's own motion data and past transfers to predict, hour by hour, whether a transfer at each turbine will stay within limits. Instead of a yes/no from a general wave height, planners see a window per turbine and per vessel, and the model learns from every logged transfer.
ideas.who_pays: Service companies pay per vessel per month during the season, about 800 EUR.
ideas.exists_detail: We built the model on 41 days of historic transfer logs and motion data from one service company. It called 88% of go/no-go decisions correctly, against 71% for the wave-height rule they use now. We have had 12 conversations with planners, and two service companies wrote letters of intent for a test in the 2027 season.

ideas.title: Fish welfare score from pen cameras
ideas.problem: Fish farms don't have a good way to measure fish welfare day to day.
ideas.who_has_it: Fish farmers.
ideas.solution: Use AI to analyse video of how the fish swim and give each pen a welfare score.

ideas.title: Marknadsplats för overallmärken
ideas.problem: Studerande samlar märken till sina studentoveraller men det är svårt att hitta och byta märken från andra städer.
ideas.who_has_it: Studerande i Finland och Sverige som har studentoverall.
ideas.solution: En app där man kan köpa, sälja och byta overallmärken med andra studerande.
ideas.who_pays: Vi tar 5 % av varje köp.

ideas.title: Bladderwrack extract as a natural preservative
ideas.problem: Natural cosmetics makers want to drop synthetic preservatives, but the plant-based options are expensive and mostly imported. Bladderwrack, a brown seaweed that grows all along the Baltic coast, contains compounds that slow down microbial growth.
ideas.who_has_it: Small Nordic natural cosmetics makers.
ideas.solution: We extract the active compounds with a water-ethanol process and test them in creams and shampoos.
ideas.who_pays: Cosmetics companies would buy the extract.
ideas.exists_detail: In a course project we got a crude extract that stopped bacterial growth in two of three lab tests. We have not talked to any cosmetics companies yet.

ideas.title: Meri puhtaaksi
ideas.problem: Meressä on liikaa roskaa.
ideas.who_has_it: Kaikki
ideas.solution: Keksitään jokin keino siivota meri.

ideas.title: Queue app for trucks at ferry terminals
ideas.problem: Trucks wait for hours at ferry terminals because the drivers don't know when they can board.
ideas.who_has_it: Truck drivers and haulage companies.
ideas.solution: An app that shows the queue and gives drivers a time slot.
ideas.who_pays: Haulage companies, monthly fee.

ideas.title: Microplastics trap for marina stormwater outlets
ideas.problem: Rainwater from marina car parks and boat yards carries paint flakes, tyre dust and plastic fragments into the sea through stormwater pipes. Marinas have to show what they do about it in their environmental permits, but there is no cheap device for small outlets.
ideas.who_has_it: Marinas and boat yards with stormwater outlets to the sea.
ideas.solution: A filter basket inside the stormwater well, with a coarse screen and a replaceable mat made from recycled fishing net that captures plastic and paint particles. A level sensor tells the yard when the mat needs changing.
ideas.who_pays: Marinas and boat yards buy the filter.
ideas.exists_detail: We are working on a first drawing.

ideas.title: Fibre scanner for second-hand textile sorting
ideas.problem: Textile sorting centres receive mixed clothes and can't tell blends from pure fibres when the care label is gone, so most unsellable textiles end up burned instead of recycled. Separate collection of textile waste became mandatory in 2025, and fibre recyclers only pay for sorted, known fibre. A mid-sized sorting centre handles 2,000-4,000 tonnes a year.
ideas.who_has_it: Sorting centres of textile collectors and second-hand chains, where staff sort one to two garments a second by hand.
ideas.solution: A handheld near-infrared scanner with our own model that identifies the fibre mix in two seconds, replacing manual reading of care labels, which are missing on about a third of garments. Recyclers then get bales with a known fibre content.
ideas.who_pays: Sorting centres lease the scanner for 390 EUR per month per scanner, model updates included.
ideas.exists_detail: The prototype, built from a low-cost spectrometer module, identified cotton, polyester and wool correctly in 91% of 300 test garments. In September 2026 it ran for two weeks at one sorting centre, where staff scanned 4,800 garments. We interviewed 9 sorting managers, and two centres signed letters of intent to lease 5 scanners in 2027.

ideas.title: Bokningsbar laddning för elbåtar i gästhamnar
ideas.problem: Allt fler fritidsbåtar har elmotor, men i skärgårdens gästhamnar finns oftast bara ett vanligt eluttag på bryggan. Båtfolket vet inte om de kan ladda innan de åker, och hamnen kan inte ta betalt för strömmen. Av de 120 elbåtsägare vi frågade hade 64 avstått från en längre tur på grund av laddningen.
ideas.who_has_it: Små gästhamnar i skärgården med 20-80 platser, ofta drivna av en förening eller en familj, och ägare av elbåtar och elutombordare.
ideas.solution: En laddstolpe för bryggan med egen mätare och en enkel bokningssida: båtägaren ser lediga laddplatser på kartan, bokar en tid och betalar för platsen och strömmen i samma köp. Hamnen får en månadsrapport. I dag får man fråga hamnvärden och hoppas att uttaget är ledigt.
ideas.who_pays: Hamnen hyr laddstolpen för 35 euro i månaden under säsongen och vi tar 10 % av varje laddning. Båtägaren betalar laddningen i bokningen.
ideas.exists_detail: Sommaren 2026 testade vi två laddstolpar i två gästhamnar i Åbolands skärgård i 9 veckor. Det blev 212 laddningar, ungefär 2 100 kWh. Båda hamnarna har betalat hyra och vill fortsätta nästa säsong, och tre hamnar till har hört av sig.

ideas.title: Opiskelijaravintolan biojäte hyönteisten ruoaksi
ideas.problem: Opiskelijaravintoloista jää päivittäin kymmeniä kiloja biojätettä. Nyt se menee biokaasulaitokselle, ja siitä maksetaan jätemaksua.
ideas.who_has_it: Opiskelijaravintolat ja muut suurkeittiöt.
ideas.solution: Kasvatetaan mustasotilaskärpäsen toukkia biojätteellä ja myydään toukat kalanrehuksi.

ideas.title: Photo grading of turbine blade erosion
ideas.problem: Offshore wind turbine blades wear down at the leading edge from rain and salt, which costs energy output. Inspectors take thousands of drone photos per wind farm and grade the damage by hand, which takes days.
ideas.who_has_it: Blade inspection and repair companies, and owners of offshore and coastal wind farms.
ideas.solution: A computer vision model that grades leading-edge erosion on a 1-5 scale from drone photos and ranks which blades need repair first.
ideas.who_pays: Inspection companies would pay per wind farm inspection, maybe 2,000 EUR.
ideas.exists_detail: Our model agrees with the expert labels on 82% of 600 photos from an open dataset. We haven't talked to inspection companies yet.

ideas.title: Summer cottage water clarity diary
ideas.problem: There are not enough measurements of water clarity in the archipelago in summer, especially in small bays.
ideas.who_has_it: Researchers and anyone who cares about the sea.
ideas.solution: An app where cottage owners measure water clarity with a simple Secchi disk every week and the data goes to an open map.
ideas.who_pays: Research grants or donations.

ideas.title: Plastic eating robot
ideas.problem: There is so much plastic in the sea, everyone knows this is a huge problem.
ideas.who_has_it: everyone
ideas.solution: A robot that swims around and eats the plastic. Somehow it would also recycle it.
ideas.who_pays: Governments?

ideas.title: Eelgrass seed pods for meadow restoration
ideas.problem: Eelgrass meadows on the west coast have shrunk by more than half since the 1980s, and restoration by hand with divers costs tens of thousands of euros per hectare, so very little gets restored.
ideas.who_has_it: Coastal municipalities and environmental foundations running restoration projects.
ideas.solution: Our method: biodegradable pods of clay and seaweed fibre, filled with eelgrass seeds and sediment, dropped from a boat through a simple chute. A boat crew could seed a hectare in a day instead of weeks of diving.
ideas.who_pays: Municipalities running restoration projects would buy pods per hectare, and maybe companies buying biodiversity credits.
ideas.exists_detail: We grew seeds in 3 different pod materials in aquariums for 6 weeks; 40% germinated in the best one. Nothing has been tested in the sea yet.

ideas.title: Lähikalaa suoraan kalastajalta
ideas.problem: Kuluttajat haluaisivat ostaa kotimaista kalaa, mutta kaupoissa on lähinnä tuontilohta. Pienet kalastajat myyvät saaliinsa halvalla tukkurille.
ideas.who_has_it: Rannikon pienkalastajat ja kaupunkilaiset kuluttajat.
ideas.solution: Verkkokauppa, josta voi tilata kalaa suoraan kalastajalta noutopisteeseen kerran viikossa.
ideas.who_pays: Otamme välityspalkkion jokaisesta tilauksesta.
ideas.exists_detail: Kysyimme kavereilta ja perheeltä, ja moni olisi kiinnostunut.

ideas.title: Under-ice oxygen and temperature logger
ideas.problem: Winter is a blind spot in coastal water quality monitoring: buoys are pulled out before the ice comes, and manual sampling through the ice happens maybe twice a winter. Low-oxygen events under the ice kill fish in shallow bays and at fish farms' winter sites, and nobody sees them until spring. Commercial ice-proof stations cost 8,000-15,000 EUR each.
ideas.who_has_it: Fish farms that keep stock over winter in coastal bays, and the consultancies that do water monitoring for municipalities and industrial permits.
ideas.solution: A sealed logger that hangs on a rope through a drilled hole, measures dissolved oxygen and temperature every 30 minutes and sends the data daily over a low-power radio network to a small mast on shore. Parts cost about 1,400 EUR, compared with 8,000 EUR or more for today's ice-proof stations, so a farm can afford several.
ideas.who_pays: Fish farms buy the logger (target price 2,600 EUR) plus a data subscription of 25 EUR per month per logger. Monitoring consultancies would rent them for the winter season.
ideas.exists_detail: Three loggers spent the winter of 2025-2026 under the ice in two bays, December to April (118 days). Two worked the whole time; one radio failed in February. We interviewed 6 fish farms and 3 monitoring consultancies, and one farm has agreed to be a pilot partner and host 4 loggers this winter.

ideas.title: Vetykäyttöinen yhteysalus saaristoon
ideas.problem: Saariston yhteysalukset käyttävät dieseliä ja tuottavat paljon päästöjä. Pelkkä akkukäyttö ei riitä pitkille reiteille talvella.
ideas.who_has_it: Saariston yhteysalusliikenne.
ideas.solution: Selvitämme, voisiko vetypolttokennoja käyttää yhteysaluksissa ja mistä vety saataisiin.
ideas.who_pays: Valtio ja julkiset tuet.
ideas.exists_detail: Kirjoitamme aiheesta kandidaatintyötä.

ideas.title: Pump-out station status map for leisure boats
ideas.problem: Leisure boats are banned from emptying toilet wastewater into the sea, but pump-out stations are often broken or hard to find, so some boaters empty their tanks anyway. On a summer weekend thousands of boats are out in the archipelago.
ideas.who_has_it: Boat owners with toilets, and the marinas and municipalities that maintain the pump-out stations.
ideas.solution: A sensor on each pump-out station and an app that shows on a map whether it works, how full its tank is and how long the queue is. Boaters can report a problem with one tap.
ideas.who_pays: Marinas pay for the sensor; the app is free for boaters.
ideas.exists_detail: We surveyed boaters at our home marina and most had found a broken pump-out station last season.

ideas.title: Points app for beach litter picking
ideas.problem: Litter ends up on beaches and it is hard to motivate volunteers to pick it up regularly.
ideas.who_has_it: Beach volunteers, families and cities.
ideas.solution: A mobile app where you collect points and badges for picking litter on beaches. You photograph the full bag and the app checks it.
ideas.who_pays: Sponsors pay to show their logo in the app.
